column5: Imagine the temperature dropped to minus one hundred degrees.
You are standing by a river in a city, on a mild autumn afternoon.
Frost creeps over the trees and the cars.
The river starts to freeze at its edges.
As cold as a winter night in Siberia.
Your breath would freeze into tiny ice crystals the moment it leaves your mouth.
Bare skin would freeze within minutes.
Drivers leave their cars and run.
Colder than any weather station on Earth has ever recorded.
In this cold, steel turns brittle.
The bridge shrinks by more than a foot.
The city stands silent, frozen in a single afternoon.
And nothing outside would move again until the warmth returned.
